column3: The Hebrew does not explicitly say “again”; it has “spoke” and “saying to them.”
The Hebrew introduces the permitted creature with singular “this living creature”; BSB uses plural “these ones.”
The Hebrew repeats the cleaving image in “cleaving a cleft of hooves”; BSB says “completely divided.”
The Hebrew joins the cud-chewing and hoof-dividing categories with “and”; BSB uses “or” and adds “only” to each category.
The Hebrew uses singular “their carcass”; BSB uses plural “their carcasses.”
The Hebrew repeats the eating instruction at the end and uses singular “fin” and “scale”; BSB gives the instruction once with plural “fins and scales.”
The Hebrew uses singular “fin” and “scale”; BSB uses plural “fins and scales.”
The Hebrew uses singular “their carcass”; BSB uses plural “their carcasses.”
The Hebrew uses singular “fin” and “scale”; BSB uses plural “fins and scales.”
The Hebrew repeats “according to its kind” after each of the four named creatures; BSB gives “any kind” once for the list.
The Hebrew says “every flying swarming thing”; BSB adds “other” to the insects.
The Hebrew addresses the people as “you” becoming unclean by these creatures; BSB makes the creatures the subject that “will make you unclean.”
The Hebrew says carrying “from their carcass,” without an explicit “one”; BSB says picking up “one of their carcasses.”
The Hebrew joins the undivided-hoof and non-ruminating descriptions with “and”; BSB uses “or.”
